item.title: API connections
item.description:
A connection and an endpoint are separate. One connection (base URL and auth) is reused by many endpoints.

@create api asks for the name, the base URL, and the auth. When Settings has environments or customers, the form asks for those too. A new connection starts on the header choice. Changing only the environment or the customer does not require another test after the current values have already passed.

Test connection sends GET to the base URL. For a new connection, any HTTP status, including 401 or 404, enables Save. DNS failure, connection refused, timeout, or a failed token request does not. When you edit a saved one, Save is enabled as soon as you change a field; testing first is optional.

item.title: Browse and edit
item.description:
Library in the jump list, @library, or Cmd+Shift+L (Ctrl+Shift+L on Windows and Linux) lists everything saved: MCP servers, API connections, endpoints, OpenAI connections, SSH connections (Pro), and collections. SSH rows also have Connect.

Filter by name or by kind. The counts on the chips are what is on this machine.

item.title: Build a workflow
item.description:
Workflows are a Pro page for a sequence you run again. First enable Settings → Experimental → Workflows; it is off by default. A block runs code, a code file, a saved HTTP endpoint, an MCP tool, or an OpenAI-compatible model. A decision picks one branch. A loop repeats a frame. The same file is the page and the YAML.

This is separate from a collection runbook, a Markdown runbook, and a repo runbook. Those stay as they are.

item.title: Commands
item.description:
termorq-cli is a Pro-only companion tool. Its commands are listed here for Pro builds; the CLI has no edition switch. See the Free and Pro feature breakdown for app features.

@ opens the command list in the prompt block. Type to filter command names. The matching letters are underlined. Cmd+Shift+F (Ctrl+Shift+F on Windows and Linux) matches letters in order anywhere in the name. Press it again to match the typed text as a block. Entries from commands.yaml follow these built-ins. @history is always available and is not a line in that file.

item.title: Connections
item.description:
SSH connections are a Pro feature (ssh.connections in features.yml). Termorq speaks SSH itself, through the Rust russh library, so Windows does not need OpenSSH installed.

Create one link

@create ssh
@ssh new

Both open the same form.

Field What it takes
Name Unique, ignoring case. It becomes the tab title and the shell pill (SSH: prod-web)
Host A name or an IP address. Pasting deploy@10.0.0.5:2222 fills user, host, and port
Port 22 by default
User The account to log in as
Authentication Private key file, ssh-agent, or Password
Private key file OpenSSH or PEM key. ~/ is expanded. Browse… opens a file picker
Key passphrase / Password Stored in the OS keychain only. Blank on edit keeps the stored one. Forget the stored … clears it
Start in folder Optional. The shell starts with cd into it
Jump host Optional bastion: host, port, and user (blank uses the user above). The same authentication is used for both hops
Local port forwards Optional, one per line: 8080:localhost:80 or 5432:db.internal:5432. See sessions and files

Save keeps it. Save and connect also opens it in a new tab.

item.title: Install Termorq
item.description:
Termorq is a Windows desktop app. Install the Free app from the Microsoft Store. There is no separate Pro listing: upgrade to Pro in the app when you need it, by selecting a Pro feature or opening License from the jump list (Ctrl+J) and choosing Try or buy Pro. See Free vs Pro for what each includes and how the trial works.

Termorq Free · upgrade to Pro in the app

After installation, open Termorq from the Windows Start menu. Microsoft Store delivers app updates.

item.title: Model connections
item.description:
Pro — Model connections are a Pro feature. Upgrade in the app.

@create openai
@openai

@create openai asks for a name, a provider, an endpoint, a model or deployment, an API key, and an optional system prompt.

Provider What you fill in
Azure OpenAI The resource endpoint, the deployment name, and the key. This is the default. Existing connections stay Azure
OpenAI or compatible A base URL (blank means https://api.openai.com/v1), a model, and a key sent as a Bearer token. The key is optional for a local server

Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and a gateway work as the compatible base URL. Both Azure URL styles are accepted: an endpoint that contains /openai/v1, and a classic deployment host.

item.title: Notes and Note workspaces
item.description:
Open Notes from the app rail or press Ctrl+Shift+N. On macOS, press Cmd+Shift+N. Notes fills the full window width. Choose Terminal in the Notes header to return to the terminal. Pressing Esc does not close Notes; Esc can still dismiss a Notes dialog or menu.

Notes keeps your Markdown in Note workspaces. A workspace is a named folder with a provider:

Provider Folder Free limit
Local Any folder on this computer 2
Obsidian An Obsidian vault (a folder with an .obsidian folder) 1
OneDrive A folder the OneDrive desktop app syncs, such as ~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Contoso/Notes or %UserProfile%\OneDrive\Notes 1
Google Drive A folder Google Drive for desktop syncs, such as ~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-you@example.com/My Drive/Notes or G:\My Drive\Notes 1

Each workspace is a tab across the top of Notes. The tab shows the provider’s logo and the workspace name; hover it to see the provider and the full folder path. The status line under an open note shows the same logo. Each workspace remembers its own open folder, note, filters, and view. The left sidebar stacks folders above the file list; drag its divider to resize it, or focus the divider and press the arrow keys. The sidebar width is remembered when you leave Notes.

item.title: On this machine
item.description:
A secret is a value. A name, a {{placeholder}}, and a vault reference are not. The app stores the value in the OS keychain and keeps the name in the file you might commit.

The keychain link

API keys, bearer tokens, basic passwords, client secrets, the OpenAI key, the MCP Azure client secret, and stdio env values whose names look like secrets use the OS keychain. The service name is termorq.

item.title: Open, save, status, close
item.description:
Team workspace is a Pro feature. The @workspace commands are available in Pro builds; Free builds keep local definitions and collections.

A team workspace is a folder in a git checkout. The app reads and writes <folder>/.ai-terminal/ and never runs git commit or git push.

@workspace open ~/src/acme-apis
@workspace
@workspace status
@workspace save
@workspace close

@workspace with no verb is status. Settings → Team workspace → Open folder is the same open. workspace in the command list opens the same commands.

item.title: Preferences
item.description: Open Settings with Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS), from the jump list, or by selecting the avatar. The cursor starts in Search all settings. Choose a category on the left; the right pane shows only that category. AI contains Report and Skills, and Forges contains Watchers. Selecting a parent shows only its own settings; selecting a nested section shows only that subsection. The navigation adapts to narrow windows, where categories scroll horizontally.

item.title: Run a collection
item.description:
termorq-cli is available in Pro builds only. It runs saved collections without opening Termorq and provides commands for listing, checking, calling, and running them. The CLI has no edition flag or runtime switch.

termorq-cli runs a saved collection without opening Termorq. It uses the same HTTP calls, variables, response checks, and captures as the app. Version 0.25.0 prints termorq-cli 0.25.0.

The screenshots on this page are the real binary, taken against a sample workspace at /tmp/acme-apis. That workspace points Users API at mock://users, the app’s offline demo host, so nothing left the machine. A secret named in the prompt is shown as …. The value never appears in the output.

item.title: Servers
item.description:
@create mcp is one form and three transports.

Transport You provide
HTTP The endpoint. No credentials, or an optional OAuth client id for servers that do not register clients
Azure client credentials Tenant id, client id, client secret, scope
stdio Command, arguments, working directory, and env

When Settings has environments or customers, the form asks for those too. A new server starts on the header choice. Changing only the environment or the customer does not require another test after the current values have already passed.

item.title: The prompt
item.description:
You type in one place, on the line after the latest output. The first characters decide what runs. The accent caret follows the insertion point as you edit the line. The folder is on the footer.

item.title: The shelf
item.description: Collections are lines you already run: a shell line, an @endpoint call, or an @tool call. Collections in the jump list, or Cmd+Shift+B (Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows and Linux), opens the shelf in the terminal column and hides the prompt. Press the shortcut again, or Esc, to return.

item.title: Capture a session as a Workflow
item.description:
Pro — Capturing a session as a Workflow is a Pro feature. Upgrade in the app.

Use Capture session from the @ command list, type @capture, or press Ctrl+Alt+R (Ctrl+Shift+R is an alternate on Windows and Linux where AltGr occupies Ctrl+Alt; macOS uses Cmd+Option+R). Capture is Pro and applies to the current tab. Ask the AI in the prompt, run a shell command, call a saved endpoint, or call an MCP tool as usual. Start capture before the actions you want to include.

item.title: Ask the model
item.description:
Pro — @chat, Ask, Agent, @explain, # lines and @agent need Termorq Pro. Upgrade in the app.

Each of these uses the OpenAI connection selected on the current tab. Nothing is sent when that pill says none.

@chat link

@chat <question> sends the question with the newest scrollback, up to about 8,000 characters, secrets masked. The tab remembers the last 20 turns. After each answer you see the tokens in and out and the chat’s running total. They are marked ≈ when the provider does not report usage. @chat on its own shows the total. @chat clear starts again.

item.title: Auth
item.description:
@create api offers seven auth kinds. The secret fields follow the kind. A blank secret on a later edit keeps the stored one.

Kind What you fill in Where the secret lives
None Base URL only Nowhere
API key Header name, default X-Api-Key, and the key Keychain, or a vault reference
Bearer The token Keychain, or a vault reference
Basic Username and password Password in the keychain, or a vault reference
Client credentials Azure tenant id, client id, client secret, scope Client secret in the keychain, or a vault reference
OAuth (browser) Authorization URL, token URL, client id, optional client secret Tokens in memory. Optional secret in the keychain
OAuth (device code) Token URL, device URL, client id, optional client secret Tokens in memory. Optional secret in the keychain

Client credentials are the Azure app-only flow: the app asks Entra for a token with the tenant, the client id, and the secret, then sends that token on the call.

item.title: Forges
item.description:
Settings → Forges connects Termorq to GitHub (github.com or GitHub Enterprise Server), GitLab (gitlab.com or a self-managed instance) or Azure DevOps (an organisation and, optionally, a project). Type @create forge at the prompt to open the same form, or search Settings for “forge”, “gitlab” or “token”.

  1. Pick the provider card.
  2. Leave Base URL blank for the cloud host, or enter your server, for example https://git.example.com. For Azure DevOps, type the organisation or paste a https://dev.azure.com/contoso/Project URL into Organisation.
  3. Paste a token. The form lists the scopes it needs:
    • GitHub: repo (read) and notifications on a classic token. That repo scope covers the private repositories the account can open. A fine-grained token covers only the repositories selected on it. See Private repositories.
    • GitLab: read_api.
    • Azure DevOps: Code (Read), Build (Read) and Work Items (Read).
  4. Select Test connection. It shows Connected as your login, or what is wrong, such as a missing scope.
  5. Select Save forge. A new connection saves only after a passing test.

item.title: Keyboard
item.description:
Cmd+/ on macOS, or Ctrl+/ on Windows and Linux, opens the shortcuts dialog. The search box at the top has focus, so you can type straight away to filter the keys, @ triggers, and call flags; matches are highlighted. Esc clears the search, then closes the dialog. Press the shortcut again to close it.

Cmd+, on macOS, or Ctrl+, on Windows and Linux, opens Settings with the cursor in its search box. Press it again to go back to the terminal. The footer hint (⌘/ help or Ctrl+/ help) opens the same dialog.

item.title: Node types and code languages
item.description:
A node on the canvas is a block in workflow YAML. Workflows are Pro and must be enabled under Settings → Experimental → Workflows. Choose the smallest block that does the job: an HTTP block for a saved endpoint, an MCP block for a saved tool, and code for a transformation that needs programming. Use AI when the task needs model judgement rather than a fixed rule.

Node types at a glance link

Editor name YAML kind Purpose When to use it
Code code Execute an inline snippet in one of seven languages. Validate input, reshape JSON, calculate a value, or adapt one service’s output for another.
Code file code_file Read a local source file and execute it with the same code runner. Keep a larger script in source control or reuse it across workflows.
Git file git The editor describes a source file in a public repository. Not currently runnable. Use Code file with a reviewed local checkout until Git file execution is implemented.
HTTP endpoint http Call a saved HTTP endpoint, or a local mock:// example. Reuse configured API connections and credentials without writing an HTTP client.
MCP tool mcp Connect to a saved MCP server and call a named tool. Use a tool’s published contract and existing transport/authentication settings.
AI ai Send a system message and prompt to a saved OpenAI-compatible model connection. Summarise, classify, or interpret information that a deterministic comparison cannot handle.
Decision decision Evaluate conditions and route to one target block. Branch on a status, count, threshold, or the presence of a value.
Loop loop Execute nested body blocks for each item, a fixed count, or while a condition holds. Process a list or repeat bounded work without copying blocks.

The editor currently offers eight types; the runner accepts the seven types other than git. A trigger starts a workflow and is configured on Triggers. It is not another runnable block type.

item.title: OAuth sign-in
item.description:
An HTTP MCP server that answers 401 is ready for sign-in. You do not fix that in the create form.

With Azure client credentials, a 401 fails the test because the server rejected an app-only token. See Azure scopes and rejected tokens, including Entra error AADSTS501461.

@mcp signin Docs
@mcp signout Docs

@mcp signin <server> finds the authorization server from the WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata link (protected resource metadata, RFC 9728), and falls back to the well-known URLs. It then reads /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414), then OpenID discovery.

item.title: Run as a runbook
item.description:
Pro — Running a collection as a runbook is a Pro feature. Upgrade in the app.

item.title: Secrets and termorq-cli
item.description:
termorq-cli is a Pro-only command-line tool. It will not start a run that needs a secret it cannot find, and it scrubs every secret it does find from the text, JSON, YAML, and JUnit it writes. The app’s keychain, export files, and workspace guard get their own chapter later.

Where the secret comes from link

For each connection a step will call, termorq-cli looks in this order:

  1. The environment variable AIT_SECRET_<CONNECTION_NAME>.
  2. The connection’s vault reference, akv://… or op://….
  3. The app’s secret store, when that store can be reached on this machine.

The variable name is the connection name in upper case, with every other character written as _. Users API becomes AIT_SECRET_USERS_API. gh-prod.v2 becomes AIT_SECRET_GH_PROD_V2.

item.title: Sessions and files
item.description:
Pro — SSH sessions need Termorq Pro. Upgrade in the app.

Open a session link

@ssh
@ssh prod-web

@ssh lists saved hosts in the prompt block, with user@host, the authentication, and any jump host. Selecting one opens a new tab named after it. The shell pill in the status strip reads SSH: prod-web, and the terminal header shows SSH · connected.

The terminal is a full xterm: vim, top, tmux, and colours work. Ctrl+Shift+C copies and Ctrl+Shift+V pastes. exit or End session closes it and the tab goes back to the local prompt.

item.title: Share a file
item.description:
The Library import menu is the front door. Save dialogs start in Downloads. Files are written with owner-only permissions.

File Holds Secret
.aitcol Collections, and optionally the endpoints and API connections those lines use, plus chosen MCP servers A bundle that includes secrets is always encrypted. A plain collections file can be encrypted too. The preview flags lines that look like they contain secrets and can mask them
.aitmcp MCP servers only, including environment and customer ids Always encrypted. Password at least 12 characters, not stored
.aitapi The ticked endpoints and the API connections they use Encrypted, and the secret is inside. OpenAI connections stay behind. Password at least 12 characters, not a common password, not one character repeated
.aitbak Settings, environments, customers, theme, collections, MCP servers, API connections, endpoints, OpenAI connections, and SSH connections, including secrets Always encrypted

Older .aitmcp and .aitapi files still import. An older file may have no environment id or customer id. The names and colours stay in Settings on this computer.

item.title: Shells
item.description:
A line that is not an @ command or a / skill runs in the tab’s shell. One command runs at a time per tab. Output streams in while it runs. Ctrl+C stops that command and everything it started.

Each tab starts one persistent interactive shell session when it opens. Termorq loads that shell’s normal startup configuration once, then sends each composer command to the same session. The working directory and exported variables therefore carry forward to later commands in that tab.

item.title: The window
item.description: The window is one prompt. A header runs across the top. Under the tabs, a full-width row names what this tab is connected to. The prompt is the next block after the output. @ and / open their lists inside that block. A footer under the terminal names the shell, the folder, and the Agent switch. The inspector is the column on the right, from under that connection row to the bottom of the window, beside the footer. HTTP, MCP, models, and collections open in the terminal column.

item.title: Todos and watchers
item.description:
Watchers are saved checks on your forge connections. While Termorq is open, each forge is checked in the background on its own schedule, and anything new lands in Todos: review requests, approvals you are required for, pull requests waiting on you, failed or finished pipelines on your branches, and work assigned to you.

  • GitHub: notifications, review requests and Actions runs. A private repository is included when the token can read it. See Private repositories.
  • GitLab: To-Do items and pipelines. A merge request, and a pipeline on its branch, can show a Datadog pill. See Datadog on GitLab.
  • Azure DevOps: pull requests where you are a reviewer or a required approver, and pipeline runs.

Open Todos with the 🔔 Todos button in the title bar (it shows the unread count), Ctrl+Shift+O (Cmd+Shift+O on macOS), Todos in the rail or the Ctrl+J jump list, or @todo at the prompt.

item.title: CI status, logs and re-run
item.description: When the current tab’s folder is a clone of a repository on one of your forge connections, the status strip shows a CI chip for the branch you are on: GitHub Actions runs, GitLab pipelines or Azure DevOps builds. It works on any branch, not only the ones your watchers cover.

item.title: Start work from a ticket
item.description: From @work, pick an issue or work item you want to work on and press Start work. Termorq suggests a branch name, finds your local clone, and shows the exact git commands before it runs anything. It always branches from the remote’s default branch, never from your local main.

item.title: Agent Skills
item.description:
Pro — Agent Skills are a Pro feature. Upgrade in the app.

Agent Skills are local SKILL.md instruction packs that Termorq can include in model requests. This is separate from the / prompt palette: those entries are Termorq prompt recipes; Agent Skills are portable instructions discovered from folders on your account.

Choose sources and defaults link

Open Settings → AI → Skills. Skill discovery is on by default and reads these folders under the selected home folder (blank uses your operating-system account home). Select Refresh after adding or changing skill files to rescan the enabled folders. Providers use distinct coloured pills; each skill shows a short description you can expand, and Common defaults starts collapsed:

item.title: Calling an endpoint
item.description:
@create endpoint asks for the connection, the name, the method, and the path. Methods are GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS. You can add query defaults, path parameters, and extra headers.

The execution target is This computer, the Invoking tab, or a Named WSL distribution and Linux user. A blank user is that distribution’s default. An endpoint saved before targets existed stays on this computer. The form shows that runtime before test and call. A run keeps the resolved computer or distribution together with the endpoint revision. The named user stays on the saved target used for that call. A collection run and Web Check do not send a WSL target from this computer. They stop instead.

item.title: Code and block examples
item.description:
Pro — Workflows are a Pro feature. Upgrade in the app.

These examples use the input and output contract. TERMORQ_INPUT contains a path. Read that file; do not parse the environment variable itself as JSON. The code runs locally, so install the language runtime listed in Node types and code languages.

Start with a Code block link

Create a workflow, switch to YAML, and paste this complete example. Return to Editor, select Echo, open its code editor, and choose Execute step. The saved sample supplies the input for this isolated test.

item.title: Files
item.description:
Two places hold state. The data folder is this machine. The workspace folder is what you commit.

Data folder link

termorq under the platform data directory.

Builds before this change used com.garrardkitchen.ai-terminal. When the app or termorq-cli starts and finds that folder, it moves the contents into termorq. If a file exists in both, the copy in termorq is kept. The old folder is then deleted. If any copy fails, the old folder is kept and the move runs again at the next start. The result goes to the OS log and to logs/app-data-migration.log:

item.title: Free and Pro feature comparison
item.description:
Termorq has Free and Pro editions. This table shows which features each edition includes. The edition is the FREE, TRIAL or PRO pill at the right of the header. Free also shows created by Garrard Kitchen on the footer. Open License from the jump list (Ctrl+J) to compare plans; the current build is highlighted.

The root features.yml manifest is the source of this feature list and the app’s feature availability. Every new feature must have an explicit plan assignment there.

item.title: Pipelines
item.description: termorq-cli is a Pro-only runner. A pipeline downloads the Pro CLI release asset for its runner, points it at the checkout with an absolute path, and passes each connection secret in from the forge’s secret store. The JUnit document is written to standard output. Warnings stay on standard error, so a skipped step does not corrupt the XML.

item.title: Report AI content
item.description:
Every AI response in the scrollback can be reported: an @explain fix, a # command, a / skill, a @chat or @agent answer, or an interpreted tool result. Reporting is in every edition. The report opens in your own email app, addressed to garrardkitchen@gmail.com, and a copy is saved on this machine first. Termorq sends nothing itself.

item.title: Sample workspace
item.description:
Download acme-apis.zip and unpack it. The workspace contains no token. Its Users API points to mock://users, an offline demo host, so calls stay on this machine.

Open it in Termorq link

Open Termorq and type the path to the unzipped folder:

@workspace open ~/Downloads/acme-apis

Change the path if you unpacked the sample somewhere else. The Users API connection needs a secret before it can run. For this offline example, any non-empty value works; it is not sent over the network. Enter it in the app so it stays in the OS keychain.

item.title: Tabs and splits
item.description:
Each tab is its own session: scrollback, folder, history, MCP servers, and OpenAI connection. Switching tabs leaves a running command where it is.

Add, rename, close link

+ opens a tab in the start folder with the saved default shell. Each tab keeps its chosen shell: changing the saved default affects new tabs and does not change existing ones. The shell-picker button immediately beside + opens a menu with Default first, followed by the other installed shells. Choose one to open and select a new tab with that shell; the saved default stays unchanged. Right-click for Rename tab… and the colour swatches. Middle-click, ×, or Close tab removes the tab. Close others closes every other tab except pinned ones, and asks once when any of them has run a command. Closing the last tab resets it.

item.title: Tools, resources, and prompts
item.description:
@tool link

@tool
@tool search
@tool search --query tea
@tool echo --message hi
@tool echo --message=hi

@tool opens the list in the prompt block, under the line you are typing. It shows the tools on the servers connected to this tab, favourites first within each server, then A→Z. When more than one server is connected, the list names the server after the description. An empty @tool with an active connection shows Disconnect on the chip. The line is the filter, and the matching letters in the name are underlined.

item.title: Run a workflow
item.description:
termorq-cli workflow is Pro. A Free binary omits these lines from --help and refuses the command with the same Pro sentence as the app. There is no edition flag.

The path after --workspace is absolute or starts with ~. The commands below use a sample checkout at ~/src/acme-apis.

termorq-cli workflow list
termorq-cli workflow list --workspace ~/src/acme-apis
termorq-cli workflow run refresh-acme-users
termorq-cli workflow runs refresh-acme-users
Command What it prints
workflow list Each workflow’s name, id, and source: included, yours, or workspace
workflow run <id> Starts that workflow and waits in this process. The desktop app does not wait
workflow runs <id> Each run directory under workflows/runs/<id>/

A file with an unknown property prints the same sentence as Save on the page, and workflow run does not start:

item.title: GraphQL and streams
item.description:
GraphQL link

Tick GraphQL on an endpoint. Its saved body is the query. The call sends POST with {"query", "variables"}.

The call’s body, or --body, is the variables JSON. A blank body sends {}.

A non-empty errors array shows as Check failed, so a check and a runbook treat it as a failure even when the HTTP status is 200.

item.title: Interactive terminal
item.description:
Each tab has one persistent interactive shell in a pseudo-terminal. Composer lines run in that session and their output is captured in the scrollback. A program that needs direct keyboard input can temporarily take over the same terminal. On Windows the terminal is ConPTY. The screen is drawn with xterm.js.

These open a terminal on their own:

item.title: The inspector
item.description:
@mcp inspect Docs

Inspect on a row in @mcp opens the same dialog. The app connects that server on the current tab first if it needs to.

Section What you see
Overview Server info, instructions, the capabilities from initialize, and the negotiated protocol version
Tools Description, pretty-printed input schema, and annotations (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open world). Call… opens the usual tool form and approval flow
Resources Resources and templates (resources/list, resources/templates/list, following nextCursor). Read shows text, or the size and MIME type of binary contents. A template’s placeholders are filled first
Prompts Arguments, then Get shows the messages
JSON-RPC log The last 200 messages sent and received for that server. Memory only. Bodies over 16 KB are cut. Secret-looking fields and the server’s stored secrets are masked. Copy copies the log as text
Ping Sends ping and shows the round trip

A section the server has no capability for shows an empty state.

item.title: Triggers, runs, and notices
item.description:
Pro — Workflows, including their triggers and runs, are a Pro feature. Upgrade in the app.

A workflow runs when you press Run, or when its selected automatic trigger fires. Choose one automatic trigger in Triggers. Switching types keeps each type’s saved settings, but only the selected type starts automatic runs. Older workflows with several configured triggers keep their settings when you choose which one is active. Manual runs stay available in the editor. Triggers run only while Termorq is open. A missed schedule is not replayed. One workflow has one active run. A second start is recorded as Skipped · already running. Two workflows may run at once.

item.title: Web Check
item.description:
Web Check is a Pro feature, powered by the Pro-only termorq-cli. In the installed Windows app, open Termorq’s notification-area icon and choose Start Web Check. On macOS, use the menu-bar or Dock menu. Choose Show Web Check output to open the local URL and pairing code, then enter that code in the browser.

The tray menu starts with the recording rows (Start recording or Stop recording and Cancel recording, then Open recording…), then a Web Check submenu (Start Web Check, Show Web Check output, Stop Web Check, Open Web Check URL). On Windows and macOS a Copy submenu, after a divider, copies the URL, pairing code, data folder path, and source folder path. Open docs (help) opens this guide, and Open Support below it opens Termorq Support (Pro support, feature requests, and bug reports), and Open Learn below that opens Termorq Learn (step-by-step tutorials). On macOS click the Termorq icon in the menu bar to open the menu; on Windows right-click the notification-area icon. Open Web Check URL and Copy Web Check URL need Web Check running.

item.title: History and plain English
item.description:
Command history link

↑ and ↓ cycle the commands on this tab when the command list and the skills list are closed. The app keeps the last 500 in command_history.json in the app data folder. Each entry is the command and at, Unix epoch milliseconds. An older file that was a plain list of strings is migrated on load (at: 0 shows as an unknown time).

item.title: Import and export
item.description:
Two exports exist. One is a file another API client can open, with secrets replaced by placeholders. The other is an encrypted file for this app, and it can carry the secret.

OpenAPI and Postman, with no secrets link

In @endpoint, tick endpoints of one API connection and choose Export OpenAPI or Export Postman. Or type:

@export openapi Users API
@export postman Users API

That exports every endpoint on the connection.

item.title: Forges
item.description: Termorq connects to the code forges you already use: GitHub (github.com or GitHub Enterprise Server), GitLab (gitlab.com or self-managed) and Azure DevOps. It shows the work assigned to you, the pull requests waiting for your review and your pipelines, and tells you when one of them needs you. It all runs in the desktop app with your own token. There are no webhooks and no Termorq server.

item.title: Find and export
item.description:
Open links and files from output link

URLs and file paths in command output have a dotted underline. Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS) opens a URL in the browser, or a file in its default app. Add Shift to show the file in Finder, Explorer, or the file manager instead. Relative paths such as src/App.tsx:12 are found from the tab’s folder, and ~/ is the home folder. A plain click still selects text. Only http and https links open.

item.title: Drop-down window
item.description:
The drop-down window is a Quake-style terminal. A global shortcut shows Termorq from the top of the screen, wherever you are, and the same shortcut hides it.

Turn it on link

Open Settings → Drop-down window and switch it On. It is off by default.

Setting Default What it does
Shortcut Cmd+Shift+Space on macOS, Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows and Linux The global key. Click the button, then press the new combination. Esc keeps the old one

A shortcut needs Ctrl, Alt or Cmd. A bare key or Shift alone is refused, because it would take ordinary typing away from every app. If another app already owns the combination, Settings shows the error and nothing is registered.

item.title: Markdown runbooks
item.description:
Markdown runbooks are a Pro feature. In Free, @md, the md row in the command list, and dropping a .md file show Markdown runbooks are available in the Pro edition. See Editions.

A runbook is often a Markdown file: a few sentences, then a command. Termorq opens that file and lets you run each code block where you read it.

Open a file link

Type @md and press Enter. A file dialog asks for a .md file.

item.title: Repo runbooks
item.description:
Repo runbooks are in Free and Pro. Explain a failed command is Pro. See Editions.

When a tab’s folder is inside a repository, Termorq looks for the tasks the repository already defines and puts them one key away. It only reads files on your disk. There is no network call, and nothing runs until you choose a task.

item.title: Recording and replay
item.description:
Session recording is a Pro feature (terminal.session_recording in features.yml). In the Free edition, Start recording, @record and the record row in the command list show “Record and replay a tab session is available in the Pro edition.” instead, and replaying a .cast is Pro too.

A recording keeps a tab’s commands and output with their timing, in the asciinema v2 .cast format. Play it back in Termorq or with asciinema play.

item.title: Inline images
item.description:
Termorq draws images where a terminal or an API sends them. Settings → Inline images turns it on or off. It is on by default.

Shell output link

Programs that use the iTerm2 inline image protocol draw in the scrollback. For example, with iTerm2’s imgcat script:

imgcat ~/Pictures/diagram.png

The image appears in place of the escape sequence. Only images marked inline=1 are drawn. A file transfer without it is dropped.

item.description:
The sidebar is this list. Each group below is a chapter.

Get started link

Install and run, build a local release, the window and its colour schemes, and the sample workspace you can run offline.

The terminal link

The prompt and command search including a multiline shell command and coloured shell output with an elapsed time, shells including an exported shell variable in an API credential or an MCP stdio environment row that the prompt does not read as you type, a call that stops before it is sent when that name is missing, and a separate value for each tab and WSL distribution that is dropped from history, exports, recordings, notifications, persisted tabs, trace, and model text, tabs and splits including opening a tab with a chosen shell, vertical tabs and tab groups, a # request that stays on this tab, and disk space from the local folder, the interactive terminal including captured output dropped when you take over a running command and Termorq commands during a program, history, find and export, inline images including a persistent shell command that keeps a TIFF, a clickable path, and one notification for a finished line, and a file dropped on an SSH terminal that is not typed into the session, Markdown runbooks including a block that runs in the file’s directory when the file has one, repo runbooks and Explain a failed command including a task that uses the tab’s host folder, recording and replay including a normal persistent-shell command, with an interactive session left as a gap note, and the drop-down window.
